transphosphorylation: GRB2 — recruited to phosphorylated tyrosines on MET (Y1356) and to SHC1; drives RAS-MAPK via SOS1. Under forced proximity, MET's kinase can also phosphorylate IL6ST ICD tyrosines, creating additional GRB2 docking sites.
SHC1 — phosphorylated by MET kinase (Y1349/Y1356 motif); recruits GRB2-SOS1. IL6ST-associated JAKs may also phosphorylate SHC1, amplifying the signal.
GAB1 — binds MET multifunctional docking site (Y1349/Y1356) directly (PMID:9242692); scaffolds PI3K and SHP2. Under forced proximity, GAB1 may also be recruited to IL6ST phosphotyrosines.
PIK3R1 — p85 regulatory subunit recruited to phosphorylated GAB1 and MET; drives PI3K-AKT-mTOR signaling.
SOS1 — recruited via GRB2 to activate RAS; the RAS-MAPK cascade is a shared output of both MET and IL6ST signaling.

STAT3 — directly phosphorylated by MET kinase (R-HSA-8875791, PMID:9440692) and by JAK1/JAK2 associated with IL6ST. The IL6ST-STAT3 axis is the canonical downstream effector; MET adds an additional STAT3 activation route.
PTPN11 (SHP2) — activated by MET (R-HSA-8865999); amplifies RAS-MAPK signaling. May also be recruited to IL6ST phosphotyrosines.
cis: JAK1 — constitutively associated with IL6ST Box1/Box2 motifs; autophosphorylates upon IL6ST clustering. Not a direct MET substrate.
JAK2 — secondary JAK associated with IL6ST; can phosphorylate IL6ST and STATs.
TYK2 — tertiary JAK family member associated with IL6ST.
CBL — E3 ubiquitin ligase that downregulates MET; recruited to MET pY1003 (not a transphosphorylation target).
excluded: PLCG1 — requires specific docking at MET pY1012/pY1313 or at IL6ST phosphotyrosines. The ~311 aa ECD asymmetry (MET ECD=908aa vs IL6ST ECD=597aa) creates a tilted intracellular geometry where PLCG1's PH-SH2-SH2-SH3 domain architecture cannot productively bridge the co-clustered ICDs. The flexible_GS8 linker (~40 Å) provides more slack than GS4 but the asymmetry still disfavors PLCG1 docking.
PLCG2 — similar domain architecture to PLCG1; same steric exclusion logic applies.

predicted_gene_rationale.up: MAPK activation via GRB2-SHC1-SOS1-RAS drives muscle structural/contractile genes (ACTA2, MYL9, MYH11, MYOM2, TAGLN, MYL6, TPM2) and NOTCH3 (satellite cell self-renewal). PI3K-AKT via GAB1-PIK3R1 upregulates CCND1 (cell cycle) and BCL2 (survival). STAT3 activation induces SOCS3 (feedback regulator). These are enriched in the P2_up (young-enriched) signature from the muscle aging atlas, consistent with the past wins pattern.
predicted_gene_rationale.down: Aged immediate-early genes (EGR1, FOS, JUN) and stress/senescence markers (TXNIP, IL32, CDKN2A, IL6) are suppressed. MYF5 (myogenic commitment) and MYH9 (non-muscle myosin) are reduced as the cell shifts toward a more mature/youthful myogenic program. OTUD1 (aged-enriched deubiquitinase) is also suppressed. This mirrors the past wins pattern where aged IEGs and inflammatory markers go down.

mechanism_narrative: MET (RTK, Tyr kinase family) and IL6ST/gp130 (type I cytokine receptor, JAK-associated) forced proximity via flexible_GS8 linker (~40 Å) is predicted to enable asymmetric bidirectional trans-signaling: MET's kinase domain phosphorylates IL6ST's intracellular tyrosines, creating STAT3 and SHC1/GRB2 docking sites, while IL6ST-associated JAK1/JAK2 transphosphorylate MET's C-tail tyrosines (Y1349/Y1356), enhancing GAB1, SHC1, and PIK3R1 recruitment. This hybrid signaling activates MAPK-ERK, PI3K-AKT-mTOR, and JAK-STAT3 pathways simultaneously. PLCG1/2 are predicted as sterically excluded due to the ~311 aa ECD asymmetry (908 vs 597 aa) creating a tilted intracellular geometry incompatible with PLCG1's multi-domain docking architecture. The biased output (MAPK↑, AKT↑, STAT3↑, PLCγ↓) promotes muscle structural gene expression and satellite cell activation while suppressing aged inflammatory IEGs — analogous to the past wins pattern but with added STAT3-mediated SOCS3 feedback.
